open_architectural_question_flagged_this: Branch protection is UNAVAILABLE on this private repo at its current plan tier (confirmed: 403 'Upgrade to GitHub Pro' on the branch-protection API) -- meaning NONE of these 20 workflows are 'required status checks' in GitHub's own enforcement sense; direct push to main is genuinely ungated by GitHub itself regardless of workflow state. This softens (but does not eliminate) the 'needs native required-check integration' reasoning used throughout this mission for self-hosting content-governance-checks.yml/skill-governance.yml/llms-generation.yml: a public-repo workflow COULD, in principle, poll on its own schedule, check out the private repo, diff against the last-seen commit, and run the same checks -- the same pattern already proven for SEO. This would trade immediate push-triggered feedback for polling latency and a more complex moving-diff-base design. This mission's destination decisions below still recommend self-hosting for these three (lower latency, already-designed, already-authorized for Phase B), but this alternative is recorded here as a genuine, not-yet-fully-evaluated option a future pass should weigh explicitly before Phase B's cutover locks it in.

UPDATE (2026-09-18): deeper investigation found the 'Stale check gate' is structurally vacuous in ANY CI context (its gitignored manifest is rebuilt from scratch immediately before being checked, every run) -- independent of and more fundamental than the duplication question below. That part of the redesign (persist the manifest across runs) is real script-level work, not attempted. WHAT WAS FIXED: regeneration now scopes to only the subdomain(s) a push actually touches instead of always --all-subdomains (verified live: --clean-output is per-subdomain-scoped, confirmed via 3 tested scratch-repo scenarios) -- directly cuts the real duplicate cost regardless of the deploy-repo question. ORIGINAL (2026-09-17) FINDING, still accurate: the duplication question is now RESOLVED, not open. Live-checked `.github/workflows/llms-generation.yml`'s own header/Summary text (states the deploy repo runs the generator again) and `gh api repos/Aspose/aspose.org-workflows/contents/.github/workflows/docs.aspose.org.yml` directly -- confirmed that workflow re-invokes `llms-generator.py` at deploy time. BUT it is workflow_dispatch-only (manual staging/production trigger, not automatic per push) and does NOT include `detect_stale_llms.py --check-only` (confirmed absent by grep) -- so the private run's fast-feedback correctness gate (catch a broken generator/content change before a human manually triggers a deploy) is NOT fully replicated publicly, even though the underlying regeneration computation is duplicated. Neither 'eliminate outright' (would drop the only fail-fast gate that exists today) nor 'leave as-is' (259 min/17.3% doing a full --all-subdomains regeneration on every content push, more work than the gate itself needs) is correct. REQUIRES_REDESIGN: keep a lightweight push-time verification step, shed the full duplicate regeneration. Confidence MEDIUM, not HIGH -- the duplication fact is now solid evidence, but the specific redesign (e.g., whether detect_stale_llms.py can validate without a full prior regenerate) was not implemented or proven in this pass.

Real cause: clone_exists() in repo_patrol.py's cmd_sweep() is a pure filesystem check against the gitignored runs/.clone_cache/, never present on a fresh checkout, zero token involvement. Fixed (Aspose/aspose.org commit 72821fbb4a) via ensure_clone() auto-clone self-heal, tested and live-verified. Already migrated PR-gated (PHB-06); the fix applies automatically since the workflow checks out Aspose/aspose.org fresh on every run. Issue #94 should be closed as a misdiagnosis, not a pending human PAT decision.

CORRECTED TWICE, same day (2026-09-18). Pass 1 disproved the HP-11 'missing pip install' theory (zero third-party imports, runs fine locally) and wrongly concluded SPLIT_BETWEEN_PRIVATE_AND_PUBLIC. Pass 2, after actually dispatching the migrated schedule leg on a real fresh checkout, found the true root cause: launch_dashboard.py's real inputs (reports/phase_state.json, reports/human-review/**, reports/**/readiness.md) are gitignored, cumulative local state (project_phase_store.py) never available in ANY fresh checkout -- public, private, self-hosted, or GitHub-hosted. Result was NO REPORT: 33/33, Gaps: 99, not the 2-gap result the local-only Pass-1 test showed. This is a data-availability defect, not a hosting-location one -- no migration destination fixes it.
